 ORDER These writ petitions are filed seeking for following reliefs:
In W.P.no.9935/2023:
(i) Declare the notifications issued by the respondents for formation of the layout called "Jayaprakash Narayana Nagar 8th Stage Layout" the Final Notification vide Annexure-H Land bearing No.36/1, measuring 02 acre 30 guntas of Kothnur Village,
Uttarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk;
(ii) Issue direction to respondents are not interfering with property right of the petitioners, vide Final Notification issued under Section 19 of the BDA Act, vide no.UDD/457/MNX/98 dated 05.04.1999, published at pages 1 to 4, part III(i) of the Karnataka Gazette dated 08.04.1999, vide Annexure-H;
(iii) Issue a writ in the nature of mandamus or direction to the respondents to consider their representation dated 03.05.2023 by the petitioners, it is marked as Annexure-J.

sentences.text: For the purpose of relief/allot, alternative site and etc.

In W.P.no.46031/2016:
(i) Issuing a writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ or order or direction to declare the Preliminary Notification no.BDA / SLAO / A6 / PR229 /
87-88 dated 23.003.1988 issued under Sub-Section(1) and (3) of Section 17 of Bangalore Development Act, 1976 (in short BDA Act) vide Annexure-A and consequently the Final Notification no.HUD 299 MNX 93 dated 19.10.1994/Final Notification dated 05.04.1999, issued under Section 19(1) of BDA Act, vide Annexure-B for the formation of Layout called "Jayaprakash Narayana Nagar 8th Stage Layout" as lapsed under Section 27 of BDA Act, in respect of petition schedule property; or NC: 2023:KHC:44927 (ii) Issue a writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ or order or direction to declare the Preliminary Notification no.BDA / SLAO / A6 / PR229 /
87-88 dated 23.003.1988 issued under Sub-Section(1) and (3) of Section 17 of Bangalore Development Act, 1976 (in short BDA Act) vide Annexure-A and consequently the Final Notification no.HUD 299 MNX 93 dated 19.10.1994/Final Notification dated 05.04.1999, issued under Section 19(1) of BDA Act, vide Mrs R V Rao vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148559110/
4 Annexure-B for the formation of Layout called "Jayaprakash Narayana Nagar 8th Stage Layout" as lapsed under Section 24(2) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, in respect of petition schedule property;
(iia) Issue writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ declaring the notifications issued for formation of layout called "Jayaprakash Narayana Nagar 8th Stage Layout" as lapsed being abandoned due to unreasonable delay in respect of petition schedule properties;
(iii) Issue a writ in the nature of mandamus or any other appropriate writ or order or direction,
directing the respondent authorities to collect betterment charges as per the provisions of the BDA Act and etc.
2.

Sri K.P. Jayasimha, learned counsel for petitioners submitted that petitioners were owners of item nos.1 to 6 of writ petition schedule properties having purchased same under sale deed at Annexures-A to F respectively.

It was submitted that said lands were acquired by respondents no.2 and 3 for formation of "Jayaprakash Narayana Nagar 8th Stage Layout"
under Preliminary Notification dated 23.03.1988 and Final Notification dated 05.04.1999.
It was submitted that award was NC: 2023:KHC:44927 passed on 31.12.2001.

However, respondents had not taken physical possession and in view of Section 27 of Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 (for short 'BDA Act')
acquisition stood lapsed.
3.

It was submitted that acquisition would be deemed lapsed in view of Section 24(2) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'RFCTLARR Act').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It was also submitted that respondent-BDA had issued an endorsement stating that petitioners' land were not suitable for acquisition as they were in developed stage.

It is also contended that acquisition notifications were violative of principles of natural justice, as petitioners were not notified of acquisition nor were they issued with any notice at time of passing award and on said ground sought for allowing writ petition.
4. On other hand, Sri Hanumantharaya Lagali, learned Additional Government Advocate for respondent no.1 and Sri K. Krishna, learned counsel for respondents for 2 and 3 sought to oppose writ petition.

Referring to statement of objections filed by respondents no.2 and 3, it was submitted NC: 2023:KHC:44927 that petitioners were purchasers of sites after issuance of acquisition notification and therefore would not be entitled to maintain writ petition challenging acquisition.
It was submitted that Preliminary Notification was issued on 23.03.1988 and Final Notification dated 05.04.1999 and petitioners had filed this writ petition after lapse of more than 35 years.

Therefore,
writ petition was liable to be dismissed on ground of delay and laches also.

5. It was further submitted that notified khatedar Sri Ramaiah and his family members had earlier filed W.P.no.22886/1999 challenging acquisition in respect of land in Sy.no.36/1 of Kothanur Village and said writ petition came to be dismissed on 15.02.2001.

Even W.P.no.22887/1999 filed Mrs R V Rao vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148559110/
5 later was also dismissed on 27.10.2003.

entities.text: Mrs R V Rao vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, notified khatedar filed application for payment of compensation.
Another person by name Dattananda Prabhu had also filed representation stating that notified khatedar had sold lands to him.
Thereafter said Sri Ramaiah filed W.P.no.23949/2001 seeking for direction to settle compensation in respect of land and for direction to BDA to pass award and pay compensation to rightful owner.

In terms of same, respondent - BDA had NC:
2023:KHC:44927 passed award on 13.12.2001 which was approved on 15.01.2002 and award amount was deposited before City Civil Court, Bangalore on 30.03.2002 vide cheque bearing no.634396 dated 27.03.2002 for a sum of Rs.7,33,873/-.
Thereafter, possession was taken on 23.01.2002 and notification under Section 16(2) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, was issued on 09.02.2012.
Thus, acquisition had been completed in accordance with law.

6. It was further submitted that subsequently some persons claiming to have purchased sites from Sri Ramaiah filed W.P.nos.2719-2714/2002 challenging award and also for consideration of their representation for deletion of lands.
By order dated 19.04.2002, writ petition was disposed of directing BDA to consider representation.
Thereafter, BDA had considered representation and issued endorsement rejecting their claims.
7. Insofar as challenge under Section 27 of BDA Act, it was submitted that petitioners allegations that BDA had not taken possession was incorrect.

It was submitted that total of 945 acres 29 guntas was acquired for "Jayaprakash Narayana Nagar 8th Stage Layout" out of which BDA took possession of NC: 2023:KHC:44927 380 acres 17 guntas and it formed layout in 217 acres 6 guntas by laying 2229 cites, 5 CA sites and 3 parks and playgrounds.
Remaining areas were not developed due to same being embroiled in litigation.
It is also stated that few lands were de-notified, but there was substantial development of lands and therefore scheme would not lapse.

8. In support of submission, learned counsel relied upon decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Delhi Development Authority v/s Manpreet Singh and Ors., in Civil Appeal no.277/2023,
disposed of on 16.01.2023.

entities.text: Delhi Development Authority v/s Manpreet Singh and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
10.

From above submission, main ground of challenge by petitioners against acquisition is that respondent - BDA had failed to take physical possession and to implement scheme and therefore as provided under Section 27 of BDA Act, scheme lapsed.
11.

It is also sought to be contended that for failure to take possession and pay compensation,
acquisition would lapse in view of Section 24(2) of RFCTLARR Act.

However, it is seen - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:44927 that petitioners' claim to have purchased items no.1 to 6 of petition schedule properties respectively on 26.04.2000, 23.04.1997, 15.03.1997, 22.01.1997, 23.04.1997 and 13.06.1997 as per sale deeds at Annexures-A to F respectively.

Mrs R V Rao vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148559110/
6 12.

entities.text: R V Rao vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, Preliminary Notification of acquisition is issued on 23.03.1988, thus petitioners are purchasers of land after initiation of acquisition.
As such, petitioners would not be entitled to question acquisition.

Even challenge against acquisition on ground of Section 24(2) of RFCTLARR Act, same would require rejection in view of authoritative pronouncement by Division Bench of this Court in case of Ananthaswamy v/s State of Karnataka and Ors., reported in AIR OnLine 2021 Kar.
6357 and in case of Indore Development Authority v/s Manoharlal, reported in 2020 (8) SCC 129 by Hon'ble Supreme Court.

entities.text:
Ananthaswamy v/s State of Karnataka and Ors., reported in AIR OnLine 2021 Kar.
6357
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Indore Development Authority v/s Manoharlal, reported in 2020 (8) SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was also contended that in Delhi Development Authority's case (supra),
it was held that subsequent purchasers would not be entitled to seek for declaration about acquisition.

13. Insofar as challenge on ground of failure to implement scheme under Section 27 of BDA Act,
respondent - BDA as stated in its statement of objections that out of total - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:44927 extent of land notified, it had taken possession of 380 acres 17 guntas and out of which, it had formed layout in 217 acres 6 guntas by laying 2229 sites and allotted.

This would indicate that there is substantial implementation of scheme hence, petitioner would not be entitled for relief on said ground also.
14.
Thus, for above said reasons writ petition stand devoid of merits and accordingly, dismissed.

It is seen that petitioners claim to have purchased petition schedule properties from original khatedar Sri Ramaiah under sale deeds dated 06.12.2003 and 08.10.2003 respectively at Annexure-D and E.
16.
And as such, reasons assigned in W.P.no.9935/2023 would apply to said writ petition also.
Hence, it is also dismissed.

Sd/-

Even W.P.no.22887/1999 filed Mrs R V Rao vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148559110/
5 later was also dismissed on 27.10.2003.
Thereafter said Sri Ramaiah filed W.P.no.23949/2001 seeking for direction to settle compensation in respect of land and for direction to BDA to pass award and pay compensation to rightful owner.
Thereafter, possession was taken on 23.01.2002 and notification under Section 16(2) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, was issued on 09.02.2012.
Thus, acquisition had been completed in accordance with law.
By order dated 19.04.2002, writ petition was disposed of directing BDA to consider representation.
Thereafter, BDA had considered representation and issued endorsement rejecting their claims.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Even challenge against acquisition on ground of Section 24(2) of RFCTLARR Act, same would require rejection in view of authoritative pronouncement by Division Bench of this Court in case of Ananthaswamy v/s State of Karnataka and Ors., reported in AIR OnLine 2021 Kar.
6357 and in case of Indore Development Authority v/s Manoharlal, reported in 2020 (8) SCC 129 by Hon'ble Supreme Court.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus, for above said reasons writ petition stand devoid of merits and accordingly, dismissed.
And as such, reasons assigned in W.P.no.9935/2023 would apply to said writ petition also.
Hence, it is also dismissed.
